protocol.description:
This protocol lets the window manager ask the compositor for visual effects on windows that river-window-management-v1 has no way to express: opacity, rounded corners, blur, shadows and a fade when a window closes. It is an extension of river (river-fx, river drawn with SceneFX) and is not part of upstream river: a window manager must work without it and use it only if the global is advertised.
Everything set through this protocol is rendering state in the sense of river-window-management-v1: it may only be changed during a manage or a render sequence, and it is applied with the next render_finish request, together with positions, borders and the rest of the rendering state.

interface.name: river_fx_v1
interface.description:
This global should only be advertised to the window manager process.
The state set for a window is reset to its defaults (fully opaque, square corners) when the window manager's river_window_v1 object for that window is destroyed, for example because the window manager exits. The same defaults apply to the rest: no blur, no shadow, no fade.

request.name: destroy
request.description: This request indicates that the client will no longer use the object. The effects already set on windows stay as they are; the effects set with set_layer_effects are removed.

request.name: set_opacity

description.summary: set the opacity of a window

request.description:
Set how opaque the content of the window is drawn. The value is a 32-bit fraction, like the colour components of river_window_v1.set_borders: 0xffffffff is fully opaque (the default), 0x00000000 fully transparent.
The borders, the decoration surfaces and the popups of the window keep their own opacity.
This request modifies rendering state and may only be made as part of a manage or render sequence, see the river_window_manager_v1 description.

request.name: set_corner_radius

description.summary: round the corners of a window

request.description:
Round the four corners of the window with the given radius, in the compositor's logical pixels. 0 (the default) draws square corners.
The radius is that of the window content. The borders set with river_window_v1.set_borders follow the content: their inner edge has this radius and their outer edge this radius plus the border width. Rounded borders are drawn on the four edges, whatever edges river_window_v1.set_borders asked for, unless the width is 0.
The corners are not rounded while the window is fullscreen.
This request modifies rendering state and may only be made as part of a manage or render sequence, see the river_window_manager_v1 description.

request.name: set_blur

description.summary: blur what is behind a window

request.description:
Blur what is drawn behind the window, as far as it shows through: where the content is translucent, because of set_opacity or because the window itself draws with transparency. The value is a 32-bit fraction: 0 (the default) is no blur, 0xffffffff the full blur of the compositor.
The blurred area is the window content, with the corners rounded as set_corner_radius asks. Nothing is blurred while the window is fullscreen.
Blur costs GPU time on every frame in which what is behind the window changes; window managers should not ask for it behind windows that are fully opaque.
This request modifies rendering state and may only be made as part of a manage or render sequence, see the river_window_manager_v1 description.

request.name: set_shadow

description.summary: draw a shadow under a window

request.description:
Draw a shadow under the window: a blurred shape of the window with its borders, with the same rounded corners, moved by the offset and spreading radius pixels beyond it. The shadow is not drawn under the window itself, so it does not show through translucent windows.
The colour is given like the one of river_window_v1.set_borders: 32-bit components, premultiplied by the alpha. An alpha of 0 (the default) removes the shadow.
There is no shadow while the window is fullscreen or clipped with river_window_v1.set_clip_box.
This request modifies rendering state and may only be made as part of a manage or render sequence, see the river_window_manager_v1 description.

arg.name: radius
arg.summary: how far the shadow spreads, in logical pixels

request.name: set_close_fade

description.summary: fade a window out when it closes

request.description:
When the window closes while it is shown, keep drawing its last content where it was and fade it out over this many milliseconds, starting from the opacity it had. 0 (the default) makes it disappear at once.
The window manager cannot do this itself: once a window is closed its river_window_v1 object is inert. The fading content is not part of any window any more: it takes no input, and its borders, shadow and blur are gone at once.
This request modifies rendering state and may only be made as part of a manage or render sequence, see the river_window_manager_v1 description.

request.name: set_layer_effects

description.summary: effects for layer surfaces with a namespace

request.description:
Set the effects of the layer-shell surfaces (bars, launchers, notifications, desktop widgets) whose namespace is the given one: those that exist now and those created later. The window manager has no object for a layer surface, so they are named by namespace. A new request for the same namespace replaces the previous one; all zeros removes the effects.
The corner radius rounds the surface, in logical pixels.
The blur is a 32-bit fraction as in set_blur. It is drawn only where the surface itself draws something, so a surface that is transparent in places (a bar made of separate pills, widgets with gaps between them) blurs only behind what it shows.
Surfaces that normally have only the wallpaper behind them (those of the bottom layer, and those of the top layer with an exclusive zone) share one blurred copy of the background layer, drawn again only when the wallpaper changes, instead of blurring on their own.
The shadow is the one of set_shadow, cast by the whole rectangle of the surface with the corner radius given here. It does not follow what the surface draws inside: it suits surfaces that are one opaque box.
This is not rendering state: it may be sent at any time and takes effect at once. These effects are removed when this river_fx_v1 object is destroyed.

request.name: set_blur_parameters
request.description:
Set how every blur of the compositor is drawn, in place of the defaults of SceneFX (3 passes, radius 5, noise 0.02, brightness 0.9, contrast 0.9, saturation 1.1).
Passes and radius make the blur wider (and dearer). The noise is a grain drawn over it, which hides banding and gives the look of frosted glass. Brightness, contrast and saturation change what is seen through the blur: 1 leaves it as it is.
This is not rendering state: it takes effect at once. The defaults come back when this river_fx_v1 object is destroyed.

request.name: set_dim
request.description:
Draw the window darker: black over it with this strength, a 32-bit fraction (0, the default, is not at all). Unlike a lower opacity, nothing shows through. It is not drawn while the window is fullscreen.
This request modifies rendering state and may only be made as part of a manage or render sequence, see the river_window_manager_v1 description.

request.name: set_close_scale

description.summary: shrink a window as it fades out

request.description:
While the window fades out after it closes (set_close_fade), also shrink it towards its centre, down to this fraction of its size at the end: a 32-bit fraction, 0xffffffff (the default) keeps its size.
This request modifies rendering state and may only be made as part of a manage or render sequence, see the river_window_manager_v1 description.

request.name: set_resize_fade

description.summary: cross-fade a window that changes size

request.description:
When the window changes size, its previous content, stretched to the new size, stays over the new one and fades out over this many milliseconds, instead of being replaced at once. 0 (the default) replaces it at once. While one fade lasts, further changes of size do not start another.
This request modifies rendering state and may only be made as part of a manage or render sequence, see the river_window_manager_v1 description.

request.name: set_layer_fade

description.summary: fade layer surfaces in and out

request.description:
The layer surfaces with this namespace fade in over this many milliseconds when they appear, and their last content fades out where it was when they go away. 0 (the default) shows and hides them at once.
Like set_layer_effects, this is not rendering state, and it is removed when this river_fx_v1 object is destroyed.

request.name: set_popup_blur
request.description:
Blur what is behind the popups of windows and of layer surfaces (menus, drop-downs, tooltips), where they are translucent. The strength is a 32-bit fraction as in set_blur; the corner radius, in logical pixels, is that of the blurred shape and should be the one the toolkit draws its menus with. Only the geometry of the popup is blurred, not the margin where it draws its own shadow.
This is not rendering state: it applies to the popups opened from now on, and is removed when this river_fx_v1 object is destroyed.
